best.rationale: y2 specifies an actionable intervention, matched random-edit controls, detection metrics, and a utility–transfer trade-off. Its logit-contrast approach reasonably adapts ref-018 to the filtering failure in ref-014, although ref-017 provides no abstract supporting token-entanglement claims. x2 offers a valuable, concrete defense experiment, but incorrectly describes ref-005 as existing adversarial training and overlooks its demonstrated transferable perturbations and physical patches. y2 connects its actual evidence, proposed difference, and evaluation more reliably.

worst.rationale: x3 largely repeats ref-002: hypothetical corporate environments, goal conflicts, insider behavior, and testing-versus-deployment self-assessment are already present. Its activation clustering lacks a specified validation method that would establish a distinct contribution. y3 incorrectly says ref-014 used only persona-style evaluations, since that reference explicitly includes misalignment. Nevertheless, tool-use trajectories provide a specific extension beyond the reported code and reasoning traces, with aligned-teacher controls and trajectory-component ablations.

diversity.rationale: X spans hidden-trait mitigation in language-model distillation, adversarial robustness of diffusion control policies, and evaluation of corporate agents. These involve substantially different systems, interventions, and outcomes. Y has meaningful internal differences—generational dynamics, data scrubbing, and tool-trajectory transfer—but all three investigate subliminal transmission through synthetic training data, anchored in ref-014. X offers the broader range of research directions.

overall.rationale: Y provides more dependable experimental starting points: y1 connects iterated amplification in ref-010 with subliminal transfer in ref-014; y2 tests a concrete defense adapted from ref-018; and y3 isolates transfer through tool-use trajectories from ref-009. Its claims of exclusive prior coverage need qualification, but the proposed differences remain identifiable. X repeatedly misstates the closest work in x2 and x3, while x1 leaves the connection between teacher-neuron correlations, data perturbations, and student parameter masking underspecified. Y better supports choosing a useful, testable project.
